Messages.Author: Reyda
Messages.Body:
I've just opened my bloodlines box....
and i'm a bit disappointed by some choices of the development team.
i don't want to go on a useless rant, i don't think my arguments are perfect
in any manner. I just want to know if i'm the only person thinking what i'm
thinking.

1
Split discipline cards :
Some split discipline cards should not have been splitted at all. Or should
have different effects. A lot of them have stupid or plain boring effects :
"Tap an untapped minion", "tap a younger vampire", "dodge" & "use your hand
or melee weapon at +1 damage" for the cost of one blood... Other cards do it
best (and some are disciplineless!). The idea is cool because you can cycle
them when you don't have the corresponding vampire in play, but anyway some
are so weak you don't want to include them in any deck.

2
Nagaraja ?
This clan is a total waste of time. What do they have ? nec, aus, dom. okay.
No new discipline. No new interesting clan ability. No political force. Only
3 vamps. Scarce. They have cool specials (except Raful) but those specials
cound have fit, say a harbinger or a baali. I'd rather have NO nagaraja in
the set and 3 more Blood brother , or 1 more of each True brujah and
Salubri, which have cool disciplines but only 3 vamps to make it.
I can't see how the Nagaraja can help us have new deck ideas (except in a
gio or malk bleed stealth, where you can make your prey discard her minion
taps...)

3
Card edition
Take a look at the vampire (crypt) card Nettie Hale, Ahrimane. Now i don't
understand how they managed to do such a mess, but no discipline symbol
appears to have the same size. Why ? is it a flaw in the software WW uses,
or some human mistake ? The disc' layout looks more and more sketchy. I know
it's a card "game" and no piece of art but...

It may sound like whining -and in fact it is, since it's a cool expansion
that will open new strategies for all players.

reyda
(still wishing there would be more Brothers to push the limit with =))

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:
Reyda wrote:

> Split discipline cards :
> Some split discipline cards should not have been splitted at all. Or should
> have different effects. A lot of them have stupid or plain boring effects :
> "Tap an untapped minion", "tap a younger vampire", "dodge" & "use your hand
> or melee weapon at +1 damage" for the cost of one blood... Other cards do it
> best (and some are disciplineless!). The idea is cool because you can cycle
> them when you don't have the corresponding vampire in play, but anyway some
> are so weak you don't want to include them in any deck.

They're intended that way, I believe. The functions that work for the new
disciplines should be very useful because it's a disadvantage to put out a
new-discipline-using vampire, so you need to do powerful things with such
vampires. However, the functions that work for existing disciplines should
*less* powerful than existing cards, not as powerful or more powerful. And
yes, that includes being less powerful than disciplines cards. Otherwise,
why would you ever use the older cards? The poor utility of the new cards
with old disciplines is the price you pay their versatility. At least you
can use them for _something_ in a pinch and not make them jam your hand.

> (still wishing there would be more Brothers to push the limit with =))

Right off hand, I'm kind of annoyed they bothered with the Blood Brothers
"circle" thing. I wonder if it's going to be hard enough using Blood
Brothers effectively without having them show up in multiple circles.
I'll withhold judgment until I actually try building and playing a BB
deck. But I've seen this kind of thing in game design before: creating a
rule that sounds good (in this case, perhaps supporting an RPG rule?) and
fun and everything but in practice only gets in the way.

Fred

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Redya wrote;

>>Split discipline cards :
Some split discipline cards should not have been splitted at all. Or should
have different effects. A lot of them have stupid or plain boring effects :
"Tap an untapped minion", "tap a younger vampire", "dodge" & "use your hand
or melee weapon at +1 damage" for the cost of one blood... Other cards do it
best (and some are disciplineless!). The idea is cool because you can cycle
them when you don't have the corresponding vampire in play, but anyway some
are so weak you don't want to include them in any deck.>>

I think that the three level discipline cards (the ones like Renewed Vigor,
Sense the Sin, and Speak with Spirits) are very well designed, perfectly
playable, and a very cool addition to the set. Yeah, the original discipline
version of most of these cards are not as powerful as similar non mixed
discipline cards (compare the aus power of Sense the Sin to, say, any other
auspex intercept card or the pot power of Vengance of Samiel to Undead
Strength), which is good, as you are trading versatility for power, which is a
Good Thing. You mix in an appropriate bloodline clan into your deck and add
some mixed discipline cards--if you have (or are acting with) the appropriate
vampire, you can use the powerful versionof the card. If not, you can use the
slightly weaker version. This makes your deck flexible, gives it versatiltiy,
and above all, makes including some bloodlines vampires *much* more viable.

>>Nagaraja ?
This clan is a total waste of time. What do they have ? nec, aus, dom. okay.
No new discipline. No new interesting clan ability. No political force. Only
3 vamps. Scarce. They have cool specials (except Raful) but those specials
cound have fit, say a harbinger or a baali. I'd rather have NO nagaraja in
the set and 3 more Blood brother , or 1 more of each True brujah and
Salubri, which have cool disciplines but only 3 vamps to make it.
I can't see how the Nagaraja can help us have new deck ideas (except in a
gio or malk bleed stealth, where you can make your prey discard her minion
taps...)>>

The same could be said for most of the bloodlines--why single out these guys?
They only take up three vamp slots and *someone* is going to want to use them.
If nothing else, they help flesh out the Giovanni.

We opened up a box last night, and were pleased with the set in general. The
new vampires and cards are pretty cool, the multi discipline cards are well
designed and effective looking (everyone is rather fond of Nose of the Hound;
Renewed Vigor, the common 5th Tradition; and that Potence/Someting Else card
that at pot gives you +2 strength for the round. Heh heh. More stackable hand
damage :-). The art is good and the graphic design is solid.

One of my immediate favorite cards of the few I own so far is Create Gargoyle.
A) they are totally cute and 2) they make Rastifarian Ghoul completely
unecessary in a Cryptic Mission deck.

>>(still wishing there would be more Brothers to push the limit with =))>>

10 isn't enough?

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
I wrote:
>>Well, sure, but again, they are a total of 3 cards in the set (and maybe a
clan
specific card or two)--they aren't *real* exciting or anything, but they are
three more vampires that share two of the three Giovanni disciplines, and
probably fit in with some other clans as well.>>

I just went and looked up the Naharaja on the Monger site, and man, those three
are really good! Who cares if they open up new an exciting strategy
opportunities or not? They are very solid, mid range vampires with good special
abilities:

-The 5 point guy with aus, dom, NEC who can take an action to burn a card in
someone's hand *easily* fits in a Giovani deck (or some Malk or Tremere decks),
providing a useful special ability.

-The 6 point guy with AUS, dom, nec, obf goes in many Malkavian decks (and some
Tremere decks), and has always useful +1 stealth built in.

-The 7 point guy with AUS, DOM, NEC, pro who fits in many Giovanni, Malk, and
Tremere decks and has a *really* good special ability.

Do the Naharaja provide new strategic angles? No, but they certainly add to
existing strategies quite well. The question is not "why did they include
vampires like the Naharaja in the set?". The real question is "Why didn't they
include *more* vampires like the Naharaja in the set?"

They are solid, efficient, mid range vampires that work well with existing
strategies, which is always a good thing.



>If there were, like, 10 different Nagaraja vampires, then sure, I'd probably

In that the questions of "What could have been included if they

between rarities to include something else.

As a lead in to discussion about how useful they could be, in the right
circumstances, it seems a useful avenue to explore.

No new discipline:
Harbingers of Skulls - aus, nec, fortitude

No political force:
How about the ability to play (auspex) intercept cards to prevent the
political action? This is limited to pred/prey without eagle's sight, but
other players (in general) seem to limit the damage to others outside of
their immediate threats. Kindred Coercion? Pulling Strings?

Only three vamps. Scarce:
Same as the Salubri and Trujah. The most expensive Nagaraja is the
cheapest Trujah.

Cool specials:
Despite Bonding and Necromancy stealth, being able to generate 1
additional stealth can come in very handy (Raful). The other two specials
are some of the most powerful I've seen.

More Blood Brothers? They already have the most vamps of any bloodline and
are probably the only bloodline that can have its own deck.

Nagaraja can add major intercept to the Giovanni...
Card retrieval to the Malks, Tremere, !Tremere and !Ventrue. I can
retrieve those low numbers of freak drives I have. They add more bleed
bounce and bleed potential to the Haribingers.

I'd like to see more of them!

Maybe in Bloodlines: The Sequel

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <u1di8ee...@news.supernews.com>, GreySeer

<e...@i.think.not> writes:
>> >I agree with you there. Necro got a good boost in FN but it still has
>> >relatively few generally useful cards.
>>
>> What do you mean by "generally useful"?
>
>It seems to lack cards that you can just put in any deck, every time I think
>Necro it's always the main focus of the deck, or the deck is focused around
>a particular Necro card ( but doesn't necessearily contain a lot of Necro
>cards ).

For a 'stealth' and bleed deck, you have the Path of Bone (not
Necromancy, but you know what I mean), Spectral Divination, Call of the
Hungry Dead for direct usage. Spiritual Intervention provides useful
combat defence (for days when you don't want to go on the offensive),
along with Ex Nihilo for distracting vampires.

Bruise decks (both bruise and bleed and general purpose combat) have
Daemonic Possession, along with Torment the Soul (difficult, but a
potentially useful source of cheap aggravated damage, aside from the
obvious Potence Burning Wrath).

Haunt provides useful location defence for any deck that's using a few
locations - The Barrens, The Mausoleum, Powerbase: Rome, Tower of London
(and you can even get the pool with the Haunt action...) are all
potentially useful locations that a Giovanni/Necromancy deck may be
packing.

Summon Soul and Whispers from the Dead are both extremely useful cards
for a number of decks. Drop them into the rest of the deck and have
another go at getting whatever you need.

Masquer provides generic intercept. In tandem with Spectral Divination,
that's +2 intercept. (And you get the Tower of London bonus again.)

Grasp the Ghostly is a metagame specific card, since it relies on other
people.

Of course, there are a few cards which need to be used in fairly large
doses - Shroud Mastery, say, along with some allies - and some cards
that *can* be used in fairly large amounts. But you don't have to play
like that, if you don't want to.

>I guess I should have said general purpose maybe. Necromancy only
>has two combat cards ( ok, Auspex doesn't have many either but some of the
>intercept cards affect the resulting combat ) and one of those isn't even
>useable in the first round.

Sure, though this does follow up the fact that both the Samedi and
Giovanni are likely to be able to do reasonably well in combat on their
own terms.

You're also ignoring Ex Nihilo which is a useful "combat" card without
being a combat card.

No discipline should be able to do everything. For instance, it's
notable that by the "Necromancy only has two combat cards" method, we
can note that Presence only has three. (Three extremely useful ones, of
course.) And Dominate - prior to Bloodlines - only had one! Absorb the
Mind and Denial of Aphrodite's Favour count kind of.

> I might be bit biased though, as neither Nec or
>Dom fit very well with Pot so your combat is very limited when it comes to
>Giovanni.

It's a case of focus. Will Dom/Nec give you the most focused powerful
combat deck in the world? No, it's very, very unlikely. So play to its
strengths, not to its weakness.
